# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.
#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)
#   sm-kicker.yml -> ci_workflow: ci.yml          (this file name)
#   machine-sm.yml -> validation-checks: ["test"] (the `test` job id below,
#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)
          PY

blocks.text:
Confirmed the integration gaps:
- No `google-services.json` in android/app/
- No google-services plugin in build.gradle
- No Google sign-in URL scheme (CFBundleURLTypes) in iOS Info.plist
- Apple entitlements file EXISTS with the capability, but it may not be referenced in the Xcode project... let me check quickly. Actually not critical — I'll note it in concerns.

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

Design specifics:

```dart
// lib/domain/app_user.dart
class AppUser {
 final String id;
 final String displayName;
 final String email;
 final AuthProvider provider; // google, apple
 toJson/fromJson
}

enum AuthProvider { google, apple }
``

```dart
// lib/services/auth_service.dart
abstract class AuthService {
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithGoogle();
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithApple();
 Future<void> signOut();
}
``

Implementation: `GoogleAppleAuthService` uses GoogleSignIn (v7 API: `GoogleSignIn.instance`, `initialize()`, `authenticate()`) and SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential. Hmm — need to be careful with the current google_sign_in API version. Let me check pub.dev for current versions. google_sign_in 7.x has the new API (`GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()`). sign_in_with_apple ^7.x: `SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential(...)`.

For google_sign_in 7.x:
```dart
final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``
Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

I need to pick versions compatible with the installed Flutter/Dart SDK (3.13.5). Latest google_sign_in is 7.x (as of late 2025, 7.1+/7.2). sign_in_with_apple 7.x. shared_preferences 2.5.x.

Since we can't fully exercise the real plugins in tests, keep the plugin wrapper thin.

Session restore flow:
- `main()`: `runApp(MyApp(authService: ..., sessionStore: ...))` — keep `main()` thin; create defaults inside `main` or in MyApp with `@visibleForTesting` injectables.
- MyApp is StatefulWidget; `initState` → `_restoreSession()` reads SessionStore.rememberedUser(); if present → set user; else → needLogin. Splash while loading.

Sign-out: HomePage calls auth service signOut + sessionStore.clear → navigates back to login.

Let me now check the actual latest package versions to pin in pubspec. Rather than guessing, use `flutter pub add google_sign_in sign_in_with_apple shared_preferences` — it resolves latest compatible and writes pubspec automatically. 

Then write tests first (RED), then implement (GREEN).

Order of TDD steps (pragmatic, verifiable):
1. Add deps.
2. Write test/widget_test.dart replacement + new tests. Actually — write test for AppUser serialization first, run (fails — no AppUser), implement. Then session store test, implement. Then login page widget tests, implement. Then app-level restore/sign-out test, implement main.dart.

Given time constraints, I'll write tests in batches but genuinely run them to see RED before implementing each unit. Let me be efficient: implement in 3 TDD cycles:

Cycle 1: AppUser model + SessionStore (persistence logic) — pure Dart unit tests.
Cycle 2: LoginPage widget (buttons, toggle, platform convention, sign-in tap persists session).
Cycle 3: App root session restore + sign-out returns to login (widget tests with fakes).

Check bash_jobs note: flutter test runs can take a while — run in background if >2min. `flutter test` on this small project should be ~30-60s. `flutter pub get` first.

# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)

Confirmed the integration gaps:
- No `google-services.json` in android/app/
- No google-services plugin in build.gradle
- No Google sign-in URL scheme (CFBundleURLTypes) in iOS Info.plist
- Apple entitlements file EXISTS with the capability, but it may not be referenced in the Xcode project... let me check quickly. Actually not critical — I'll note it in concerns.

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

Design specifics:

```dart
// lib/domain/app_user.dart
class AppUser {
 final String id;
 final String displayName;
 final String email;
 final AuthProvider provider; // google, apple
 toJson/fromJson
}

enum AuthProvider { google, apple }
``

```dart
// lib/services/auth_service.dart
abstract class AuthService {
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithGoogle();
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithApple();
 Future<void> signOut();
}
``

Implementation: `GoogleAppleAuthService` uses GoogleSignIn (v7 API: `GoogleSignIn.instance`, `initialize()`, `authenticate()`) and SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential. Hmm — need to be careful with the current google_sign_in API version. Let me check pub.dev for current versions. google_sign_in 7.x has the new API (`GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()`). sign_in_with_apple ^7.x: `SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential(...)`.

For google_sign_in 7.x:
```dart
final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``
Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

I need to pick versions compatible with the installed Flutter/Dart SDK (3.13.5). Latest google_sign_in is 7.x (as of late 2025, 7.1+/7.2). sign_in_with_apple 7.x. shared_preferences 2.5.x.

Since we can't fully exercise the real plugins in tests, keep the plugin wrapper thin.

Session restore flow:
- `main()`: `runApp(MyApp(authService: ..., sessionStore: ...))` — keep `main()` thin; create defaults inside `main` or in MyApp with `@visibleForTesting` injectables.
- MyApp is StatefulWidget; `initState` → `_restoreSession()` reads SessionStore.rememberedUser(); if present → set user; else → needLogin. Splash while loading.

Sign-out: HomePage calls auth service signOut + sessionStore.clear → navigates back to login.

Let me now check the actual latest package versions to pin in pubspec. Rather than guessing, use `flutter pub add google_sign_in sign_in_with_apple shared_preferences` — it resolves latest compatible and writes pubspec automatically. 

Then write tests first (RED), then implement (GREEN).

1. Add deps.
2. Write test/widget_test.dart replacement + new tests. Actually — write test for AppUser serialization first, run (fails — no AppUser), implement. Then session store test, implement. Then login page widget tests, implement. Then app-level restore/sign-out test, implement main.dart.

Cycle 1: AppUser model + SessionStore (persistence logic) — pure Dart unit tests.
Cycle 2: LoginPage widget (buttons, toggle, platform convention, sign-in tap persists session).
Cycle 3: App root session restore + sign-out returns to login (widget tests with fakes).

name: CI

  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))

          for f in files:

Confirmed the integration gaps:
- No `google-services.json` in android/app/
- No google-services plugin in build.gradle
- No Google sign-in URL scheme (CFBundleURLTypes) in iOS Info.plist
- Apple entitlements file EXISTS with the capability, but it may not be referenced in the Xcode project... let me check quickly. Actually not critical — I'll note it in concerns.

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

Design specifics:

```dart
// lib/domain/app_user.dart
class AppUser {
 final String id;
 final String displayName;
 final String email;
 final AuthProvider provider; // google, apple
 toJson/fromJson
}

enum AuthProvider { google, apple }
``

```dart
// lib/services/auth_service.dart
abstract class AuthService {
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithGoogle();
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithApple();
 Future<void> signOut();
}
``

Implementation: `GoogleAppleAuthService` uses GoogleSignIn (v7 API: `GoogleSignIn.instance`, `initialize()`, `authenticate()`) and SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential. Hmm — need to be careful with the current google_sign_in API version. Let me check pub.dev for current versions. google_sign_in 7.x has the new API (`GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()`). sign_in_with_apple ^7.x: `SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential(...)`.

For google_sign_in 7.x:
```dart
final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``
Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

I need to pick versions compatible with the installed Flutter/Dart SDK (3.13.5). Latest google_sign_in is 7.x (as of late 2025, 7.1+/7.2). sign_in_with_apple 7.x. shared_preferences 2.5.x.

- MyApp is StatefulWidget; `initState` → `_restoreSession()` reads SessionStore.rememberedUser(); if present → set user; else → needLogin. Splash while loading.

Sign-out: HomePage calls auth service signOut + sessionStore.clear → navigates back to login.

        required: false

        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.
#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)
#   sm-kicker.yml -> ci_workflow: ci.yml          (this file name)
#   machine-sm.yml -> validation-checks: ["test"] (the `test` job id below,
#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)
          PY

Confirmed the integration gaps:
- No `google-services.json` in android/app/
- No google-services plugin in build.gradle
- No Google sign-in URL scheme (CFBundleURLTypes) in iOS Info.plist
- Apple entitlements file EXISTS with the capability, but it may not be referenced in the Xcode project... let me check quickly. Actually not critical — I'll note it in concerns.

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

Design specifics:

```dart
// lib/domain/app_user.dart
class AppUser {
 final String id;
 final String displayName;
 final String email;
 final AuthProvider provider; // google, apple
 toJson/fromJson
}

enum AuthProvider { google, apple }
``

```dart
// lib/services/auth_service.dart
abstract class AuthService {
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithGoogle();
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithApple();
 Future<void> signOut();
}
``

Implementation: `GoogleAppleAuthService` uses GoogleSignIn (v7 API: `GoogleSignIn.instance`, `initialize()`, `authenticate()`) and SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential. Hmm — need to be careful with the current google_sign_in API version. Let me check pub.dev for current versions. google_sign_in 7.x has the new API (`GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()`). sign_in_with_apple ^7.x: `SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential(...)`.

For google_sign_in 7.x:
```dart
final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``
Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

I need to pick versions compatible with the installed Flutter/Dart SDK (3.13.5). Latest google_sign_in is 7.x (as of late 2025, 7.1+/7.2). sign_in_with_apple 7.x. shared_preferences 2.5.x.

- MyApp is StatefulWidget; `initState` → `_restoreSession()` reads SessionStore.rememberedUser(); if present → set user; else → needLogin. Splash while loading.

Sign-out: HomePage calls auth service signOut + sessionStore.clear → navigates back to login.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:

#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input

# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||

      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:

    types: [assigned]

        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true

Senior Developer Engineer ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Story ticket ready for development]) --> READ_INPUT["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ_INPUT --> PREFLIGHT{"⚠️ STEP 0 input-completeness pre-flight:
any missing attachment / reference / contradiction?"} PREFLIGHT -->|Highlights - missing input| ASK["Post ONE comment asking for the missing items +
write outputs/needs-input.md + STOP (no code changes)"] ASK --> END_ASK([End - needs input - no PR]) PREFLIGHT -->|Clean| PARENT["Read parent epic context if present:
- input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md — business rules
- input/TICKET/parent_context_sa.md — technical design
- input/TICKET/parent_context_vd.md — visual design"] PARENT --> ANALYZE["Analyze requirements — every acceptance criterion must be addressed"] ANALYZE --> ARCH["Understand existing codebase patterns, architecture, and test structure"] ARCH --> PRINCIPLES["Apply OOP principles: SRP, OCP, DI, Encapsulation, Composition over inheritance"] PRINCIPLES --> TDD["Follow TDD approach — see tdd_approach.md"] TDD --> TEST_LOC["Write TDD tests in the standard unit-test tree only
— Flutter/Dart: test/
— NEVER in testing/ (owned by test-automation agents)"] TEST_LOC --> IMPLEMENT["Implement source code and unit tests following existing patterns"] IMPLEMENT --> DOCS["Update documentation ONLY if ticket explicitly requires it"] DOCS --> RUN["Run all unit tests — MUST pass before finishing"] RUN --> PASS{Tests pass?} PASS -->|No| FIX["Fix failures and re-run tests"] FIX --> RUN PASS -->|Yes| POSTCHECK{"Integration readiness check:
does the feature depend on external setup
the repo does not contain?"} POSTCHECK -->|Gaps found| CONCERNS["Write outputs/concerns.md:
what is missing + what is needed to make it work"] CONCERNS --> GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] POSTCHECK -->|Self-sufficient| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| GUARD["⚠️ COMPLETION GUARD — prove work landed BEFORE writing the summary:
git fetch origin main && git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline
EMPTY result = work did NOT land — re-do or resume the work,
NEVER report done from session memory or main's tip"] IGNORE --> GUARD GUARD -->|Diff shows your commits| SUMMARY["Write concise PR description to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] GUARD -->|Empty diff| REDO["Re-do or resume the work — verify the working dir,
git log, git stash list.
If the fix is genuinely already on the base branch,
prove it (git log origin/main -- grep) before any
'no changes needed' conclusion"] REDO --> IMPLEMENT SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles branch, commit and PR]) ``` ## ⚠️ STEP 0 — INPUT COMPLETENESS PRE-FLIGHT (surface scan, before ANY work) Right after reading the input files, run a QUICK (surface-level) go/no-go scan of the ticket — title, description, and comments authored by humans. Do NOT deep-analyze. Flag only highlights that would force you to ASSUME: - The ticket references an attachment, image, screenshot, logo, design file, or external resource that is NOT present in the ticket context. - Referenced credentials, environment details, or access are missing. - Essential statements contradict each other. If there ARE highlights — do NOT implement. Instead: > **TEMPORARY COLLISION WORKAROUND — remove later.** The machine currently > runs under the same GitHub identity as the human reporter > (SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN = the repo owner; `ai-teammate` is not yet a > separate collaborator account), so author login cannot tell the agent's > own question from a human reply. Once the machine runs under a dedicated > identity, drop this marker requirement AND the marker check in the > dispatch gate (dmtools-agentic-workflows scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh). 1. Post ONE comment on the ticket asking for exactly the missing items. Be specific; propose nothing, assume nothing. The comment MUST end with this exact machine marker line (it tells the pipeline this comment is the agent's own question, not a human reply): `` 2. Write `outputs/needs-input.md` listing the missing items (same content as the comment). 3. Make NO code changes and stop. The pipeline labels the ticket `ai_questions_asked` and ends the leg without a PR. If there are NO highlights — continue with the normal flow. **Hard rules — these overrides are NOT yours to make:** - NEVER generate, synthesize…

Senior Developer Engineer ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Story ticket ready for development]) --> READ_INPUT["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ_INPUT --> PREFLIGHT{"⚠️ STEP 0 input-completeness pre-flight:
any missing attachment / reference / contradiction?"} PREFLIGHT -->|Highlights - missing input| ASK["Post ONE comment asking for the missing items +
write outputs/needs-input.md + STOP (no code changes)"] ASK --> END_ASK([End - needs input - no PR]) PREFLIGHT -->|Clean| PARENT["Read parent epic context if present:
- input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md — business rules
- input/TICKET/parent_context_sa.md — technical design
- input/TICKET/parent_context_vd.md — visual design"] PARENT --> ANALYZE["Analyze requirements — every acceptance criterion must be addressed"] ANALYZE --> ARCH["Understand existing codebase patterns, architecture, and test structure"] ARCH --> PRINCIPLES["Apply OOP principles: SRP, OCP, DI, Encapsulation, Composition over inheritance"] PRINCIPLES --> TDD["Follow TDD approach — see tdd_approach.md"] TDD --> TEST_LOC["Write TDD tests in the standard unit-test tree only
— Flutter/Dart: test/
— NEVER in testing/ (owned by test-automation agents)"] TEST_LOC --> IMPLEMENT["Implement source code and unit tests following existing patterns"] IMPLEMENT --> DOCS["Update documentation ONLY if ticket explicitly requires it"] DOCS --> RUN["Run all unit tests — MUST pass before finishing"] RUN --> PASS{Tests pass?} PASS -->|No| FIX["Fix failures and re-run tests"] FIX --> RUN PASS -->|Yes| POSTCHECK{"Integration readiness check:
does the feature depend on external setup
the repo does not contain?"} POSTCHECK -->|Gaps found| CONCERNS["Write outputs/concerns.md:
what is missing + what is needed to make it work"] CONCERNS --> GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] POSTCHECK -->|Self-sufficient| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| GUARD["⚠️ COMPLETION GUARD — prove work landed BEFORE writing the summary:
git fetch origin main && git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline
EMPTY result = work did NOT land — re-do or resume the work,
NEVER report done from session memory or main's tip"] IGNORE --> GUARD GUARD -->|Diff shows your commits| SUMMARY["Write concise PR description to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] GUARD -->|Empty diff| REDO["Re-do or resume the work — verify the working dir,
git log, git stash list.
If the fix is genuinely already on the base branch,
prove it (git log origin/main -- grep) before any
'no changes needed' conclusion"] REDO --> IMPLEMENT SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles branch, commit and PR]) ``` ## ⚠️ STEP 0 — INPUT COMPLETENESS PRE-FLIGHT (surface scan, before ANY work) Right after reading the input files, run a QUICK (surface-level) go/no-go scan of the ticket — title, description, and comments authored by humans. Do NOT deep-analyze. Flag only highlights that would force you to ASSUME: - The ticket references an attachment, image, screenshot, logo, design file, or external resource that is NOT present in the ticket context. - Referenced credentials, environment details, or access are missing. - Essential statements contradict each other. If there ARE highlights — do NOT implement. Instead: > **TEMPORARY COLLISION WORKAROUND — remove later.** The machine currently > runs under the same GitHub identity as the human reporter > (SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN = the repo owner; `ai-teammate` is not yet a > separate collaborator account), so author login cannot tell the agent's > own question from a human reply. Once the machine runs under a dedicated > identity, drop this marker requirement AND the marker check in the > dispatch gate (dmtools-agentic-workflows scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh). 1. Post ONE comment on the ticket asking for exactly the missing items. Be specific; propose nothing, assume nothing. The comment MUST end with this exact machine marker line (it tells the pipeline this comment is the agent's own question, not a human reply): `` 2. Write `outputs/needs-input.md` listing the missing items (same content as the comment). 3. Make NO code changes and stop. The pipeline labels the ticket `ai_questions_asked` and ends the leg without a PR. If there are NO highlights — continue with the normal flow. **Hard rules — these overrides are NOT yours to make:** - NEVER generate, synthesize…

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:

    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf

    types: [assigned]

        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice

        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false

Confirmed the integration gaps:
- No `google-services.json` in android/app/
- No google-services plugin in build.gradle

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

Design specifics:

```dart
// lib/domain/app_user.dart
class AppUser {
 final String id;
 final String displayName;
 final String email;
 final AuthProvider provider; // google, apple
 toJson/fromJson
}

enum AuthProvider { google, apple }
``

```dart
// lib/services/auth_service.dart
abstract class AuthService {
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithGoogle();
 Future<AppUser?> signInWithApple();
 Future<void> signOut();
}
``

Implementation: `GoogleAppleAuthService` uses GoogleSignIn (v7 API: `GoogleSignIn.instance`, `initialize()`, `authenticate()`) and SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential. Hmm — need to be careful with the current google_sign_in API version. Let me check pub.dev for current versions. google_sign_in 7.x has the new API (`GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()`). sign_in_with_apple ^7.x: `SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential(...)`.

For google_sign_in 7.x:
```dart
final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``
Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

I need to pick versions compatible with the installed Flutter/Dart SDK (3.13.5). Latest google_sign_in is 7.x (as of late 2025, 7.1+/7.2). sign_in_with_apple 7.x. shared_preferences 2.5.x.

Sign-out: HomePage calls auth service signOut + sessionStore.clear → navigates back to login.

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string

#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x

Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## - input/TICKET/parent_context_vd.md — visual design"] PARENT --> ANALYZE["Analyze requirements — every acceptance criterion must be addressed"] ANALYZE --> ARCH["Understand existing codebase patterns, architecture, and test structure"] ARCH --> PRINCIPLES["Apply OOP principles: SRP, OCP, DI, Encapsulation, Composition over inheritance"] PRINCIPLES --> TDD["Follow TDD approach — see tdd_approach.md"] TDD --> TEST_LOC["Write TDD tests in the standard unit-test tree only
— Flutter/Dart: test/

does the feature depend on external setup
the repo does not contain?"} POSTCHECK -->|Gaps found| CONCERNS["Write outputs/concerns.md:
what is missing + what is needed to make it work"] CONCERNS --> GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] POSTCHECK -->|Self-sufficient| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| GUARD["⚠️ COMPLETION GUARD — prove work landed BEFORE writing the summary:

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

abstract class AuthService {

}

```dart
final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``
Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string

#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x

Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

Senior Developer Engineer ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ## input_context_reading.md ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph INPUT_ORDER["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read input files FIRST before anything else"] I0["find input/ -type f | sort — list all available files"] I1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, deployment constraints, approved frameworks"] I2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/request.md — ticket description, requirements, solution design, diagrams"] I3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — existing discussion, prior decisions, linked info"] I4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/existing_questions.json — answered questions = binding requirements"] I5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — specifications already downloaded"] I6["6️⃣ Check for images in input/TICKET/ — *.png *.jpg *.gif *.svg"] I7["7️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent-KEY.md — parent story summary, description, ACs"] I8["8️⃣ If present: input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md / sa.md / vd.md — BA/SA/VD context"] I0 --> I1 --> I2 --> I3 --> I4 --> I5 --> I6 --> I7 --> I8 end subgraph CONFLUENCE_RULE["Confluence pages in input/ — READ THEM, don't re-fetch"] C1["✅ DO: read input/TICKET/confluence/PageName.md"] C2["❌ DON'T: call dmtools confluence_* to re-fetch pages already in input/"] C3["✅ DO: read image files in input/TICKET/confluence/ — they are attachments from that page"] end subgraph ATTACH_RULE["Attachments — check before fetching via API"] A1["Search glob 'input/**/*.png' and 'input/**/*.jpg' — find pre-downloaded images"] A2["If image found locally → analyze it directly, no API call needed"] A3["If attachment NOT in input/ → use dmtools confluence_get_content_attachments "] A1 --> A2 A1 -->|not found| A3 end subgraph DMTOOLS_RULE["When to use dmtools for external data"] D1["ONLY if you need data NOT already in input/"] D2["dmtools jira_get_ticket KEY, dmtools confluence_search QUERY, etc."] D3["See instructions/common/dmtools_cli.md for full reference"] end INPUT_ORDER --> CONFLUENCE_RULE --> ATTACH_RULE --> DMTOOLS_RULE ``` ## general_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Story ticket ready for development]) --> READ_INPUT["⚠️ MANDATORY: Read ALL input files FIRST — see instructions/common/input_context_reading.md"] READ_INPUT --> PREFLIGHT{"⚠️ STEP 0 input-completeness pre-flight:
any missing attachment / reference / contradiction?"} PREFLIGHT -->|Highlights - missing input| ASK["Post ONE comment asking for the missing items +
write outputs/needs-input.md + STOP (no code changes)"] ASK --> END_ASK([End - needs input - no PR]) PREFLIGHT -->|Clean| PARENT["Read parent epic context if present:
- input/TICKET/parent_context_ba.md — business rules
- input/TICKET/parent_context_sa.md — technical design
- input/TICKET/parent_context_vd.md — visual design"] PARENT --> ANALYZE["Analyze requirements — every acceptance criterion must be addressed"] ANALYZE --> ARCH["Understand existing codebase patterns, architecture, and test structure"] ARCH --> PRINCIPLES["Apply OOP principles: SRP, OCP, DI, Encapsulation, Composition over inheritance"] PRINCIPLES --> TDD["Follow TDD approach — see tdd_approach.md"] TDD --> TEST_LOC["Write TDD tests in the standard unit-test tree only
— Flutter/Dart: test/
— NEVER in testing/ (owned by test-automation agents)"] TEST_LOC --> IMPLEMENT["Implement source code and unit tests following existing patterns"] IMPLEMENT --> DOCS["Update documentation ONLY if ticket explicitly requires it"] DOCS --> RUN["Run all unit tests — MUST pass before finishing"] RUN --> PASS{Tests pass?} PASS -->|No| FIX["Fix failures and re-run tests"] FIX --> RUN PASS -->|Yes| POSTCHECK{"Integration readiness check:
does the feature depend on external setup
the repo does not contain?"} POSTCHECK -->|Gaps found| CONCERNS["Write outputs/concerns.md:
what is missing + what is needed to make it work"] CONCERNS --> GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] POSTCHECK -->|Self-sufficient| GITSTATUS["Run git status and review every new/modified file"] GITSTATUS --> SECRETS{Sensitive or untracked non-code files present?} SECRETS -->|Yes| IGNORE["Add appropriate patterns to .gitignore"] SECRETS -->|No| GUARD["⚠️ COMPLETION GUARD — prove work landed BEFORE writing the summary:
git fetch origin main && git log origin/main..HEAD --oneline
EMPTY result = work did NOT land — re-do or resume the work,
NEVER report done from session memory or main's tip"] IGNORE --> GUARD GUARD -->|Diff shows your commits| SUMMARY["Write concise PR description to outputs/response.md — see output_rules.md"] GUARD -->|Empty diff| REDO["Re-do or resume the work — verify the working dir,
git log, git stash list.
If the fix is genuinely already on the base branch,
prove it (git log origin/main -- grep) before any
'no changes needed' conclusion"] REDO --> IMPLEMENT SUMMARY --> END([End — post-processing handles branch, commit and PR]) ``` ## ⚠️ STEP 0 — INPUT COMPLETENESS PRE-FLIGHT (surface scan, before ANY work) Right after reading the input files, run a QUICK (surface-level) go/no-go scan of the ticket — title, description, and comments authored by humans. Do NOT deep-analyze. Flag only highlights that would force you to ASSUME: - The ticket references an attachment, image, screenshot, logo, design file, or external resource that is NOT present in the ticket context. - Referenced credentials, environment details, or access are missing. - Essential statements contradict each other. If there ARE highlights — do NOT implement. Instead: > **TEMPORARY COLLISION WORKAROUND — remove later.** The machine currently > runs under the same GitHub identity as the human reporter > (SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN = the repo owner; `ai-teammate` is not yet a > separate collaborator account), so author login cannot tell the agent's > own question from a human reply. Once the machine runs under a dedicated > identity, drop this marker requirement AND the marker check in the > dispatch gate (dmtools-agentic-workflows scripts/teammate-dispatch-gate.sh). 1. Post ONE comment on the ticket asking for exactly the missing items. Be specific; propose nothing, assume nothing. The comment MUST end with this exact machine marker line (it tells the pipeline this comment is the agent's own question, not a human reply): `` 2. Write `outputs/needs-input.md` listing the missing items (same content as the comment). 3. Make NO code changes and stop. The pipeline labels the ticket `ai_questions_asked` and ends the leg without a PR. If there are NO highlights — continue with the normal flow. **Hard rules — these overrides are NOT yours to make:** - NEVER generate, synthesize…

#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.

name: 'AI Teammate'

      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,

Plan per ticket gh-12:

**Scope:**
1. Login page: Google sign-in button, Apple sign-in button (per platform conventions — Apple on iOS, Google on both)
2. Use `google_sign_in` and `sign_in_with_apple` packages
3. "Remember me" toggle: persist signed-in account locally (`shared_preferences`) and auto-restore on app start, skipping login page
4. Sign-out action that clears remembered account

**ACs:**
- Login page renders with both sign-in buttons and remember-me toggle
- Signed-in account persists across app restarts when remember-me is on
- Sign-out returns the user to the login page
- Widget tests cover the login page and the session restore logic
- `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` pass

Architecture design:
- `lib/domain/app_user.dart` — simple user model (id, displayName, email, provider)
- `lib/services/auth_service.dart` — abstract auth interface + implementation wrapping google_sign_in / sign_in_with_apple; injectable
- `lib/services/session_store.dart` — abstract persistence (shared_preferences-backed); injectable for tests
- `lib/ui/login_page.dart` — login page with Google button (always), Apple button (iOS only), remember-me toggle
- `lib/ui/home_page.dart` — signed-in home showing account info + sign-out button
- `lib/main.dart` — app root; restores session on start (async), shows login or home

Key testability considerations: platform-detection for Apple button (defaultTargetPlatform), and auth flows must be mockable. shared_preferences in widget tests needs `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({})`.

Note: `google_sign_in` and `sign_in_with_apple` require platform setup (Android google-services config, iOS entitlements) — that's the "integration readiness" concern to write to outputs/concerns.md: the repo does not contain `google-services.json`, `GoogleService-Info.plist`, Apple entitlements (`sign_in_with_apple` capability), URL schemes, etc. The code will compile and tests pass, but real sign-in won't work on device without that config. # AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:

#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)

#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring

          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)

blocks.text:
I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

Platform convention for Apple button: show only on iOS/macOS — use `defaultTargetPlatform` (widget tests can override with `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`). `SignInWithAppleButton` from the package for the Apple button; Google button custom-styled (the google_sign_in 7.x package has a `GoogleSignInButton` in google_sign_in_widgets.dart! Let me check: `lib/widgets.dart` exists in google_sign_in 7.2.0 — there's `GoogleSignInButton`. Let me verify).

Actually I saw `lib/widgets.dart` in the google_sign_in package. Let me check what it provides — if it has a ready button, use it (follow established patterns). But it may require a controller/instance wiring that complicates fakes. A custom button is more predictable and testable. Let me check quickly.
