Only an avatar widget, no button. I'll build custom-styled buttons (Google white button with "G" logo text, Apple black button via `SignInWithAppleButton` from the sign_in_with_apple package — that package has a `SignInWithAppleButton` widget in `lib/src/widgets`).

For testability, I'll use my own button widgets with stable keys/labels. For Apple, the package's `SignInWithAppleButton` is a standard convention; it has `onPressed`. In widget tests I can find it by type or wrap it. Simpler and more robust for tests: my own `AppleSignInButton` and `GoogleSignInButton` widgets in `ui/buttons.dart` that render platform-appropriate styling and take `onPressed`. But the ticket says "per platform conventions — Apple on iOS". Using the official `SignInWithAppleButton` matches Apple's Human Interface Guidelines (Apple requires their branded button). I'll use `SignInWithAppleButton` (black style) from the package and a custom Google button following Google's branding (white bg, colored G).

Hmm — for widget tests, finding `SignInWithAppleButton` works by type: `find.byType(SignInWithAppleButton)`. And tapping: `tester.tap(find.byType(SignInWithAppleButton))` — its internal gesture detector will fire onPressed. That works.

Google button: custom `OutlinedButton.icon` with `key: Key('google_sign_in_button')` or semantic label "Sign in with Google" / "Continue with Google".

Now the fake auth in tests: `FakeAuthService implements AuthService` with programmable results.

SessionController with ChangeNotifier — testable with fake store (in-memory).

Let me now write the TDD tests first. To keep momentum I'll write the full test suite first (they'll fail to compile = RED), then implement, then iterate until green. That's the pragmatic batch-TDD approach. Actually — the guidelines want RED first then GREEN per behavior. Compile-failure counts as RED for the first cycle. I'll run tests after writing tests to confirm failure, then implement.

Files to write. First the tests:

**test/domain/app_user_test.dart**
- toJson/fromJson roundtrip (google user)
- roundtrip (apple user)
- fromJson with missing displayName → empty string? Decide: displayName is String? (nullable — Apple may not give name on re-auth). Keep displayName String? and email String? (Apple email can be null on re-auth; Google email is non-null). For simplicity: `displayName` and `email` nullable, `id` required, `provider` required.
- equality test.

**test/services/session_store_test.dart**
- save + load returns user and remember flag
- clear empties
- with real SharedPreferences: `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({})`.

**test/services/session_controller_test.dart**
- restore with remembered user → signedIn(user)
- restore with nothing → signedOut
- signInWithGoogle(remember=true) → signedIn + persisted; verify store contains
- signInWithGoogle(remember=false) → signedIn, store empty
- signInWithApple similar (2 items rule: cover both providers)
- signOut → signedOut + store cleared
- canceled sign-in (null from service) → stays signedOut, nothing persisted

**test/ui/login_page_test.dart**
- renders Google button + Apple button + remember-me switch (default off... or default on? Spec: "Remember me" toggle; default off is conventional)
- Apple button hidden on Android platform (debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = TargetPlatform.android)
- Apple button shown on iOS
- Google button always shown on both platforms
- tap Google sign-in → controller.signInWithGoogle called with remember value
- toggle remember-me, tap Google → remember true persisted
- tapping Apple on iOS → controller.signInWithApple

**test/ui/home_page_test.dart**
- shows user info (name/email)
- sign-out button → controller.signOut called

**test/widget_test.dart** (app-level)
- app starts with no session → login page shown (after restore completes)
- app starts with remembered session → home shown, login skipped
- sign-out from home → returns to login page and store cleared

For app-level tests, inject fakes into MyApp. Design: `MyApp({required SessionController? controller...})`. Better: `DmToolsApp({AuthService? authService, SessionStore? sessionStore})` — creates real SessionController if not provided. In main(): `runApp(DmToolsApp(authService: GoogleAppleAuthService(), sessionStore: SharedPreferencesSessionStore()))`.

SessionController as ChangeNotifier with AnimatedBuilder/ListenableBuilder in the app widget.

Let me now write all test files, run to confirm RED, then implement.

One design decision for SessionStore interface:

```dart
abstract class SessionStore {
 Future<void> save(AppUser user);
 Future<AppUser?> load();
 Future<void> clear();
}
``

The "remember me" semantic: save() only called when remember is on; clear() on sign-out. Load returns remembered user. Good.

AuthProvider enum with name for serialization: `AuthProvider.google.name`.

AppUser:

```dart
class AppUser {
 const AppUser({required this.id, required this.provider, this.displayName, this.email});
 final String id;
 final AuthProvider provider;
 final String? displayName;
 final String? email;
 // ==, hashCode, copyWith, toJson, fromJson
}
``

fromJson must handle provider unknown → throw ArgumentError. Test that.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/

 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:

    types: [assigned]

name: CI

on:
  push:

permissions:

jobs:
  test:

4. UI:

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

Platform convention for Apple button: show only on iOS/macOS — use `defaultTargetPlatform` (widget tests can override with `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`). `SignInWithAppleButton` from the package for the Apple button; Google button custom-styled (the google_sign_in 7.x package has a `GoogleSignInButton` in google_sign_in_widgets.dart! Let me check: `lib/widgets.dart` exists in google_sign_in 7.2.0 — there's `GoogleSignInButton`. Let me verify).

Actually I saw `lib/widgets.dart` in the google_sign_in package. Let me check what it provides — if it has a ready button, use it (follow established patterns). But it may require a controller/instance wiring that complicates fakes. A custom button is more predictable and testable. Let me check quickly.

Only an avatar widget, no button. I'll build custom-styled buttons (Google white button with "G" logo text, Apple black button via `SignInWithAppleButton` from the sign_in_with_apple package — that package has a `SignInWithAppleButton` widget in `lib/src/widgets`).

For testability, I'll use my own button widgets with stable keys/labels. For Apple, the package's `SignInWithAppleButton` is a standard convention; it has `onPressed`. In widget tests I can find it by type or wrap it. Simpler and more robust for tests: my own `AppleSignInButton` and `GoogleSignInButton` widgets in `ui/buttons.dart` that render platform-appropriate styling and take `onPressed`. But the ticket says "per platform conventions — Apple on iOS". Using the official `SignInWithAppleButton` matches Apple's Human Interface Guidelines (Apple requires their branded button). I'll use `SignInWithAppleButton` (black style) from the package and a custom Google button following Google's branding (white bg, colored G).

Hmm — for widget tests, finding `SignInWithAppleButton` works by type: `find.byType(SignInWithAppleButton)`. And tapping: `tester.tap(find.byType(SignInWithAppleButton))` — its internal gesture detector will fire onPressed. That works.

Google button: custom `OutlinedButton.icon` with `key: Key('google_sign_in_button')` or semantic label "Sign in with Google" / "Continue with Google".

Now the fake auth in tests: `FakeAuthService implements AuthService` with programmable results.

SessionController with ChangeNotifier — testable with fake store (in-memory).

Let me now write the TDD tests first. To keep momentum I'll write the full test suite first (they'll fail to compile = RED), then implement, then iterate until green. That's the pragmatic batch-TDD approach. Actually — the guidelines want RED first then GREEN per behavior. Compile-failure counts as RED for the first cycle. I'll run tests after writing tests to confirm failure, then implement.

Files to write. First the tests:

**test/domain/app_user_test.dart**
- toJson/fromJson roundtrip (google user)
- roundtrip (apple user)
- fromJson with missing displayName → empty string? Decide: displayName is String? (nullable — Apple may not give name on re-auth). Keep displayName String? and email String? (Apple email can be null on re-auth; Google email is non-null). For simplicity: `displayName` and `email` nullable, `id` required, `provider` required.
- equality test.

**test/services/session_store_test.dart**
- save + load returns user and remember flag
- clear empties
- with real SharedPreferences: `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({})`.

**test/services/session_controller_test.dart**
- restore with remembered user → signedIn(user)
- restore with nothing → signedOut
- signInWithGoogle(remember=true) → signedIn + persisted; verify store contains
- signInWithGoogle(remember=false) → signedIn, store empty
- signInWithApple similar (2 items rule: cover both providers)
- signOut → signedOut + store cleared
- canceled sign-in (null from service) → stays signedOut, nothing persisted

**test/ui/login_page_test.dart**
- renders Google button + Apple button + remember-me switch (default off... or default on? Spec: "Remember me" toggle; default off is conventional)
- Apple button hidden on Android platform (debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = TargetPlatform.android)
- Apple button shown on iOS
- Google button always shown on both platforms
- tap Google sign-in → controller.signInWithGoogle called with remember value
- toggle remember-me, tap Google → remember true persisted
- tapping Apple on iOS → controller.signInWithApple

**test/ui/home_page_test.dart**
- shows user info (name/email)
- sign-out button → controller.signOut called

**test/widget_test.dart** (app-level)
- app starts with no session → login page shown (after restore completes)
- app starts with remembered session → home shown, login skipped
- sign-out from home → returns to login page and store cleared

For app-level tests, inject fakes into MyApp. Design: `MyApp({required SessionController? controller...})`. Better: `DmToolsApp({AuthService? authService, SessionStore? sessionStore})` — creates real SessionController if not provided. In main(): `runApp(DmToolsApp(authService: GoogleAppleAuthService(), sessionStore: SharedPreferencesSessionStore()))`.

SessionController as ChangeNotifier with AnimatedBuilder/ListenableBuilder in the app widget.

Let me now write all test files, run to confirm RED, then implement.

One design decision for SessionStore interface:

```dart
abstract class SessionStore {
 Future<void> save(AppUser user);
 Future<AppUser?> load();
 Future<void> clear();
}
``

The "remember me" semantic: save() only called when remember is on; clear() on sign-out. Load returns remembered user. Good.

AuthProvider enum with name for serialization: `AuthProvider.google.name`.

AppUser:

```dart
class AppUser {
 const AppUser({required this.id, required this.provider, this.displayName, this.email});
 final String id;
 final AuthProvider provider;
 final String? displayName;
 final String? email;
 // ==, hashCode, copyWith, toJson, fromJson
}
``

fromJson must handle provider unknown → throw ArgumentError. Test that.

No prebuilt Google button — I'll build custom-styled branded buttons. Architecture planned: `domain/app_user.dart`, `services/` (auth, store, controller), `ui/` (login, home). Starting TDD — **RED phase**: writing the failing tests first.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/

 services/session_store_test.dart

 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:

    types: [assigned]

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.
#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)
#   sm-kicker.yml -> ci_workflow: ci.yml          (this file name)
#   machine-sm.yml -> validation-checks: ["test"] (the `test` job id below,
#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)
          PY

4. UI:

5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

Platform convention for Apple button: show only on iOS/macOS — use `defaultTargetPlatform` (widget tests can override with `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`). `SignInWithAppleButton` from the package for the Apple button; Google button custom-styled (the google_sign_in 7.x package has a `GoogleSignInButton` in google_sign_in_widgets.dart! Let me check: `lib/widgets.dart` exists in google_sign_in 7.2.0 — there's `GoogleSignInButton`. Let me verify).

Actually I saw `lib/widgets.dart` in the google_sign_in package. Let me check what it provides — if it has a ready button, use it (follow established patterns). But it may require a controller/instance wiring that complicates fakes. A custom button is more predictable and testable. Let me check quickly.
All API details confirmed. Let me check if google_sign_in ships a ready-made button widget:
{"command":"cat ~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/google_sign_in-7.2.0/lib/widgets.dart"}

Only an avatar widget, no button. I'll build custom-styled buttons (Google white button with "G" logo text, Apple black button via `SignInWithAppleButton` from the sign_in_with_apple package — that package has a `SignInWithAppleButton` widget in `lib/src/widgets`).

For testability, I'll use my own button widgets with stable keys/labels. For Apple, the package's `SignInWithAppleButton` is a standard convention; it has `onPressed`. In widget tests I can find it by type or wrap it. Simpler and more robust for tests: my own `AppleSignInButton` and `GoogleSignInButton` widgets in `ui/buttons.dart` that render platform-appropriate styling and take `onPressed`. But the ticket says "per platform conventions — Apple on iOS". Using the official `SignInWithAppleButton` matches Apple's Human Interface Guidelines (Apple requires their branded button). I'll use `SignInWithAppleButton` (black style) from the package and a custom Google button following Google's branding (white bg, colored G).

Hmm — for widget tests, finding `SignInWithAppleButton` works by type: `find.byType(SignInWithAppleButton)`. And tapping: `tester.tap(find.byType(SignInWithAppleButton))` — its internal gesture detector will fire onPressed. That works.

Google button: custom `OutlinedButton.icon` with `key: Key('google_sign_in_button')` or semantic label "Sign in with Google" / "Continue with Google".

Now the fake auth in tests: `FakeAuthService implements AuthService` with programmable results.

SessionController with ChangeNotifier — testable with fake store (in-memory).

Let me now write the TDD tests first. To keep momentum I'll write the full test suite first (they'll fail to compile = RED), then implement, then iterate until green. That's the pragmatic batch-TDD approach. Actually — the guidelines want RED first then GREEN per behavior. Compile-failure counts as RED for the first cycle. I'll run tests after writing tests to confirm failure, then implement.

Files to write. First the tests:

**test/domain/app_user_test.dart**
- toJson/fromJson roundtrip (google user)
- roundtrip (apple user)
- fromJson with missing displayName → empty string? Decide: displayName is String? (nullable — Apple may not give name on re-auth). Keep displayName String? and email String? (Apple email can be null on re-auth; Google email is non-null). For simplicity: `displayName` and `email` nullable, `id` required, `provider` required.
- equality test.

**test/services/session_store_test.dart**
- save + load returns user and remember flag
- clear empties
- with real SharedPreferences: `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({})`.

**test/services/session_controller_test.dart**
- restore with remembered user → signedIn(user)
- restore with nothing → signedOut
- signInWithGoogle(remember=true) → signedIn + persisted; verify store contains
- signInWithGoogle(remember=false) → signedIn, store empty
- signInWithApple similar (2 items rule: cover both providers)
- signOut → signedOut + store cleared
- canceled sign-in (null from service) → stays signedOut, nothing persisted

**test/ui/login_page_test.dart**
- renders Google button + Apple button + remember-me switch (default off... or default on? Spec: "Remember me" toggle; default off is conventional)
- Apple button hidden on Android platform (debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride = TargetPlatform.android)
- Apple button shown on iOS
- Google button always shown on both platforms
- tap Google sign-in → controller.signInWithGoogle called with remember value
- toggle remember-me, tap Google → remember true persisted
- tapping Apple on iOS → controller.signInWithApple

**test/ui/home_page_test.dart**
- shows user info (name/email)
- sign-out button → controller.signOut called

**test/widget_test.dart** (app-level)
- app starts with no session → login page shown (after restore completes)
- app starts with remembered session → home shown, login skipped
- sign-out from home → returns to login page and store cleared

For app-level tests, inject fakes into MyApp. Design: `MyApp({required SessionController? controller...})`. Better: `DmToolsApp({AuthService? authService, SessionStore? sessionStore})` — creates real SessionController if not provided. In main(): `runApp(DmToolsApp(authService: GoogleAppleAuthService(), sessionStore: SharedPreferencesSessionStore()))`.

SessionController as ChangeNotifier with AnimatedBuilder/ListenableBuilder in the app widget.

Let me now write all test files, run to confirm RED, then implement.

One design decision for SessionStore interface:

```dart
abstract class SessionStore {
 Future<void> save(AppUser user);
 Future<AppUser?> load();
 Future<void> clear();
}
``

The "remember me" semantic: save() only called when remember is on; clear() on sign-out. Load returns remembered user. Good.

AuthProvider enum with name for serialization: `AuthProvider.google.name`.

AppUser:

```dart
class AppUser {
 const AppUser({required this.id, required this.provider, this.displayName, this.email});
 final String id;
 final AuthProvider provider;
 final String? displayName;
 final String? email;
 // ==, hashCode, copyWith, toJson, fromJson
}
``

fromJson must handle provider unknown → throw ArgumentError. Test that.

Now write the tests. Note existing test/widget_test.dart (counter test) must be replaced — the counter app is gone.

Let me write test files now.

No prebuilt Google button — I'll build custom-styled branded buttons. Architecture planned: `domain/app_user.dart`, `services/` (auth, store, controller), `ui/` (login, home). Starting TDD — **RED phase**: writing the failing tests first.

#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input

# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||

      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:

    types: [assigned]

        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/

``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user

- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string

#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

The auth service must be injectable so widget tests never invoke real plugin calls. Use plain constructor injection with interfaces.

final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;
await googleSignIn.initialize(authEventStream: ...); // initialize once
final account = await googleSignIn.authenticate(scopeHint: ['email']);
final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x

Actually in 7.x: `GoogleSignInAccount.authentication` returns `GoogleSignInAuthentication` synchronously. And `authenticate()` throws GoogleSignInException on cancel.

For 6.x: `googleSignIn.signIn()` returns nullable GoogleSignInAccount.

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist

**Architecture:**

``
lib/

 domain/

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist

The git history was squashed — only one commit exists. So no previous login implementation to reference. I'll build from scratch following Flutter conventions.

Let me check what's available:
- Flutter version installed
- Check the .github workflows for CI to understand what commands run

Plan per ticket gh-12:

**Scope:**
1. Login page: Google sign-in button, Apple sign-in button (per platform conventions — Apple on iOS, Google on both)
2. Use `google_sign_in` and `sign_in_with_apple` packages
3. "Remember me" toggle: persist signed-in account locally (`shared_preferences`) and auto-restore on app start, skipping login page
4. Sign-out action that clears remembered account

**ACs:**
- Login page renders with both sign-in buttons and remember-me toggle
- Signed-in account persists across app restarts when remember-me is on
- Sign-out returns the user to the login page
- Widget tests cover the login page and the session restore logic
- `flutter analyze` and `flutter test` pass

Architecture design:
- `lib/domain/app_user.dart` — simple user model (id, displayName, email, provider)
- `lib/services/auth_service.dart` — abstract auth interface + implementation wrapping google_sign_in / sign_in_with_apple; injectable
- `lib/services/session_store.dart` — abstract persistence (shared_preferences-backed); injectable for tests
- `lib/ui/login_page.dart` — login page with Google button (always), Apple button (iOS only), remember-me toggle
- `lib/ui/home_page.dart` — signed-in home showing account info + sign-out button
- `lib/main.dart` — app root; restores session on start (async), shows login or home

Key testability considerations: platform-detection for Apple button (defaultTargetPlatform), and auth flows must be mockable. shared_preferences in widget tests needs `SharedPreferences.setMockInitialValues({})`.

Note: `google_sign_in` and `sign_in_with_apple` require platform setup (Android google-services config, iOS entitlements) — that's the "integration readiness" concern to write to outputs/concerns.md: the repo does not contain `google-services.json`, `GoogleService-Info.plist`, Apple entitlements (`sign_in_with_apple` capability), URL schemes, etc. The code will compile and tests pass, but real sign-in won't work on device without that config. That's exactly what the post-check wants flagged.

TDD approach: write tests first, then implement. Let me be pragmatic: I'll write the tests and implementation incrementally, running tests along the way.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  # Human replies on needs-input tickets re-arm the dev leg via the
  # factory gate (comment-resume); PR comments are filtered by the if below.
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:

#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml

name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          for f in files:

              print("ok:", f)

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier

   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart

 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

# PR CI for the DMTools machine loop.
#
# The factory stubs bind to these exact names — keep in sync when renaming:
#   machine-merge.yml / sm-kicker.yml / merge-trigger.yml
#       -> workflow_run: workflows: ['CI']       (this file's `name:`)
#   sm-kicker.yml -> ci_workflow: ci.yml          (this file name)
#   machine-sm.yml -> validation-checks: ["test"] (the `test` job id below,
#                                                    the required context)
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Validate DMTools wiring
        run: |
          node --check .dmtools/config.js
          node -e 'const fs=require("fs");for(const f of fs.readdirSync(".dmtools/runners")){JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(".dmtools/runners/"+f,"utf8"));console.log("ok:",f);}'

      - name: Validate workflow YAML
        run: |
          python3 - <<'PY'
          import glob, yaml
          files = sorted(glob.glob(".github/workflows/*.yml"))
          assert any(f.endswith("/ci.yml") for f in files), "ci.yml missing"
          for f in files:
              yaml.safe_load(open(f))
              print("ok:", f)
          PY

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

Platform convention for Apple button: show only on iOS/macOS — use `defaultTargetPlatform` (widget tests can override with `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`). `SignInWithAppleButton` from the package for the Apple button; Google button custom-styled (the google_sign_in 7.x package has a `GoogleSignInButton` in google_sign_in_widgets.dart! Let me check: `lib/widgets.dart` exists in google_sign_in 7.2.0 — there's `GoogleSignInButton`. Let me verify).

3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

final googleSignIn = GoogleSignIn.instance;

Plan of work (TDD):

1. Add dependencies: `google_sign_in`, `sign_in_with_apple`, `shared_preferences`.
2. Domain: `AppUser` model.
3. Services:
  - `AuthService` abstract + `GoogleAppleAuthService` implementation wrapping the two plugins. Injectable/fakeable.
  - `SessionStore` abstract + `SharedPreferencesSessionStore` (persist JSON of user + remember flag).
4. UI:
  - `LoginPage` (Google button always, Apple button on iOS only, remember-me toggle).
  - `HomePage` (signed-in view: account info, sign-out).
5. `main.dart`: root widget `MyApp` — restores session on start via `SessionStore`/`AuthService`, shows splash while restoring, then LoginPage or HomePage.
6. Widget tests in `test/`:
  - `login_page_test.dart`: renders both buttons + remember-me toggle; Apple button hidden on Android (platform override via `debugDefaultTargetPlatformOverride`); Google always; tapping sign-in with remember-me on persists account.
  - `session restore test`: app starts, session store has remembered account → home shown, skipping login. Sign-out clears store and returns to login.
  - `app_user_test.dart` maybe for model serialization (toJson/fromJson roundtrip).

final idToken = account.authentication.idToken; // authentication is sync getter in 7.x
``

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart
 ui/login_page_test.dart
 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Widget tree: MaterialApp → splash (CircularProgressIndicator) while restoring → LoginPage or HomePage.

I have all the API details I need. Now let me design and write the code.

**Architecture:**

``
lib/
 main.dart                — app entry, DI wiring, session restore bootstrapping
 domain/
   app_user.dart          — AppUser model + AuthProvider enum (toJson/fromJson)
 services/
   auth_service.dart      — AuthService interface + GoogleAppleAuthService impl
   session_store.dart     — SessionStore interface + SharedPreferencesSessionStore impl
   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier
 ui/
   login_page.dart        — login page (Google always, Apple on Apple platforms, remember-me)
   home_page.dart         — signed-in page with sign-out
test/
 widget_test.dart         — replaced: app bootstrapping tests
 domain/app_user_test.dart
 services/session_store_test.dart
 services/session_controller_test.dart

 ui/home_page_test.dart
``

SessionController (ChangeNotifier):
- state: SessionStatus { restoring, signedOut, signedIn }, AppUser? user
- `restore()` — reads SessionStore; if remembered user → signedIn; else signedOut
- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

**Architecture:**

``
lib/

**Architecture:**

``
lib/

**Architecture:**

``

**Architecture:**

``
lib/

**Architecture:**

``

   session_controller.dart — session state machine (restore, signIn, signOut) — ChangeNotifier

- `signInWithGoogle(bool remember)` / `signInWithApple(bool remember)` — calls AuthService; on success and remember → persist
- `signOut()` — AuthService.signOut + SessionStore.clear → signedOut

Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Also fix FakeAuthService constructor to accept gates.

blocks.text:
Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

messages.preview: Real bug found: on cancel/failure the controller stays stuck in `restoring` (infinite splash). Fixing the controller plus the two test-file issues:

blocks.text:
Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Also fix FakeAuthService constructor to accept gates.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

messages.preview: Real bug found: on cancel/failure the controller stays stuck in `restoring` (infinite splash). Fixing the controller plus the two test-file issues:

blocks.text:
Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Also fix FakeAuthService constructor to accept gates.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Also fix FakeAuthService constructor to accept gates.

blocks.text:
Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

blocks.text:
Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

blocks.text:
Found it. `SessionStatus` starts at `restoring`. The controller's `_signIn` on failure/cancel leaves status at `restoring` (never transitions to signedOut). That's a real bug: a fresh controller that fails to sign in stays "restoring" forever → the app would show the splash infinitely.

Fix in SessionController: in `_signIn`, when account == null (canceled) or on error → if status is still restoring, set it to signedOut. Cleaner: track `restore()` completion. Simplest correct: in `_signIn` catch/cancel paths: `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut`.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

Also fix FakeAuthService constructor to accept gates.

blocks.text:
Remaining failures (5):

1. **`SwitchListTile` not `Switch`** — cast in tests: `tester.widget<Switch>(...)` → change to `SwitchListTile` and check `.value`.

2. **"buttons show progress"** — `tester.widget<OutlinedButton>(...)` — "Bad state: No element": the OutlinedButton isn't found... because when busy, buttons are hidden (I show progress INSTEAD of buttons). My test expects the button to still exist but disabled. Design choice conflict. Two options: (a) keep buttons visible and disabled while busy (better UX honestly — layout doesn't jump); (b) change test.

I prefer (a): keep the buttons in the tree, disabled, and show a small progress indicator below. Change login page: don't swap out buttons; always show buttons + toggle, and when busy show progress and disable buttons.

3. **`notifies listeners`** — transitions.first expected `restoring` but got `signedOut`. Sequence: restore() → load() → notify with signedIn/signedOut. The listener fires only on notifyListeners — status is already `signedOut` at that point; `restoring` is never notified (no notify during restore start). Fix the test: first transition IS the restore result. Update expectation: first is `signedOut` (nothing remembered), then contains signedIn after sign-in, last signedOut. That matches implementation semantics (restoring is the initial state before any listener notification — splash is shown by the app because the widget reads status at build). It's fine — no code change needed, adjust test.

4. **widget_test 'session is NOT restored when remember-me was off'** — LoginPage not found after second launch. Why? Second launch: store empty (nothing saved). controller.restore() → status signedOut → LoginPage. Hmm, but `addPostFrameCallback` → restore. `pumpAndSetle` should handle. Unless... the first launch's LoginPage is still in the tree? No — expectation says LoginPage count 0.

Wait — maybe the SECOND launch kept showing... Let me think: `store.load()` on SharedMemorySessionStore — nothing was saved → null → signedOut → LoginPage shown. But found 0 LoginPages AND the error "nothing was persisted, so login is required again" at line 132: `expect(find.byType(LoginPage), findsOneWidget...)`. Also `HomePage findsNothing` passed? Order: expect LoginPage findsOneWidget (FAILED at 132). So neither login nor home?? Or home IS shown (login 0, home...). If HomePage were found, the findsNothing would fail after. Failure at line 132 is the LoginPage expect.

Hypothesis: after `pumpWidget(DmToolsApp(...))` for second launch, the OLD controller `firstLaunch` still has status signedIn, and ListenableBuilder of the OLD widget tree... no — new pumpWidget replaces the tree. New DmToolsApp state created → initState → postFrameCallback restore → pumpAndSetle runs frames → restore completes → signedOut → LoginPage renders.

Unless restore() returned early! My `restore()` guard: `if (_status != SessionStatus.restoring) return;` — new controller starts restoring → fine.

Hmm wait — actually the issue may be the FIRST controller: `firstLaunch` controller gets disposed? No.

Let me think about `SharedMemorySessionStore` — save was called? First launch: tap google (remember off) → signInWithGoogle(remember: false) → NOT saved → store empty. Good.

Second launch pumpAndSetle... Actually — `_signIn` finally → notifyListeners. But wait: does the tap in the FIRST launch actually complete sign-in? `FakeAuthService(googleResult: testUser())` → completes immediately. pumpAndSetle → HomePage shown — expected HomePage findsOneWidget — that assertion passed (line before 132 didn't fail).

So why no LoginPage on second launch? OH — I see it. `DmToolsApp` is `const DmToolsApp(sessionController: secondLaunch)`. When pumping a widget with the SAME runtimeType and no key, `pumpWidget` UPDATES the existing State rather than recreating it! The State field `_controller` is `late final` — initialized once with `widget.sessionController` (firstLaunch). On update with the new widget, `_DmToolsAppState` is REUSED (same widget type, same position) — `didUpdateWidget` not implemented, `_controller` stays firstLaunch! So the "second launch" still shows the first controller (signedIn) → HomePage. Hence LoginPage 0.

Fix: give the app state a distinct Key for each launch in the test: `DmToolsApp(key: UniqueKey(), sessionController: ...)`. With different keys, State is recreated. That's the cleanest fix in the test.

Also — `didUpdateWidget` handling in production: not needed for real usage (single launch). Keys in test are fine.

5. Also the earlier `signOut` in home page test passed.

- login_page.dart: keep buttons visible+disabled while busy; show progress as extra element. Use SwitchListTile.value assertions in tests.
- login_page_test: `tester.widget<SwitchListTile>(...)`, cast for OutlinedButton — with buttons always visible, the busy test finds OutlinedButton. `.onPressed` null when disabled.
- session_controller_test: fix transitions expectation.
- widget_test: add `key: UniqueKey()` per launch — need import of foundation/material (material imported; UniqueKey is in foundation, re-exported by material? `UniqueKey` is in foundation; material exports foundation's key classes? material.dart exports foundation.dart? No — material exports `foundations` basics like Key via painting/basic types... `UniqueKey` comes from package:flutter/foundation.dart; material.dart does export it indirectly? Actually `flutter/material.dart` exports `package:flutter/foundation.dart`? It doesn't. But `widgets.dart` exports foundation. MaterialApp is in material which re-exports widgets. UniqueKey is exported via widgets? Hmm: `flutter/widgets.dart` has `export 'package:flutter/foundation.dart' show ...UniqueKey...`? To be safe, import foundation in widget_test.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.

blocks.text:
Remaining failures (5):

1. **`SwitchListTile` not `Switch`** — cast in tests: `tester.widget<Switch>(...)` → change to `SwitchListTile` and check `.value`.

2. **"buttons show progress"** — `tester.widget<OutlinedButton>(...)` — "Bad state: No element": the OutlinedButton isn't found... because when busy, buttons are hidden (I show progress INSTEAD of buttons). My test expects the button to still exist but disabled. Design choice conflict. Two options: (a) keep buttons visible and disabled while busy (better UX honestly — layout doesn't jump); (b) change test.

I prefer (a): keep the buttons in the tree, disabled, and show a small progress indicator below. Change login page: don't swap out buttons; always show buttons + toggle, and when busy show progress and disable buttons.

3. **`notifies listeners`** — transitions.first expected `restoring` but got `signedOut`. Sequence: restore() → load() → notify with signedIn/signedOut. The listener fires only on notifyListeners — status is already `signedOut` at that point; `restoring` is never notified (no notify during restore start). Fix the test: first transition IS the restore result. Update expectation: first is `signedOut` (nothing remembered), then contains signedIn after sign-in, last signedOut. That matches implementation semantics (restoring is the initial state before any listener notification — splash is shown by the app because the widget reads status at build). It's fine — no code change needed, adjust test.

4. **widget_test 'session is NOT restored when remember-me was off'** — LoginPage not found after second launch. Why? Second launch: store empty (nothing saved). controller.restore() → status signedOut → LoginPage. Hmm, but `addPostFrameCallback` → restore. `pumpAndSetle` should handle. Unless... the first launch's LoginPage is still in the tree? No — expectation says LoginPage count 0.

Wait — maybe the SECOND launch kept showing... Let me think: `store.load()` on SharedMemorySessionStore — nothing was saved → null → signedOut → LoginPage shown. But found 0 LoginPages AND the error "nothing was persisted, so login is required again" at line 132: `expect(find.byType(LoginPage), findsOneWidget...)`. Also `HomePage findsNothing` passed? Order: expect LoginPage findsOneWidget (FAILED at 132). So neither login nor home?? Or home IS shown (login 0, home...). If HomePage were found, the findsNothing would fail after. Failure at line 132 is the LoginPage expect.

Hypothesis: after `pumpWidget(DmToolsApp(...))` for second launch, the OLD controller `firstLaunch` still has status signedIn, and ListenableBuilder of the OLD widget tree... no — new pumpWidget replaces the tree. New DmToolsApp state created → initState → postFrameCallback restore → pumpAndSetle runs frames → restore completes → signedOut → LoginPage renders.

Unless restore() returned early! My `restore()` guard: `if (_status != SessionStatus.restoring) return;` — new controller starts restoring → fine.

Hmm wait — actually the issue may be the FIRST controller: `firstLaunch` controller gets disposed? No.

Let me think about `SharedMemorySessionStore` — save was called? First launch: tap google (remember off) → signInWithGoogle(remember: false) → NOT saved → store empty. Good.

Second launch pumpAndSetle... Actually — `_signIn` finally → notifyListeners. But wait: does the tap in the FIRST launch actually complete sign-in? `FakeAuthService(googleResult: testUser())` → completes immediately. pumpAndSetle → HomePage shown — expected HomePage findsOneWidget — that assertion passed (line before 132 didn't fail).

So why no LoginPage on second launch? OH — I see it. `DmToolsApp` is `const DmToolsApp(sessionController: secondLaunch)`. When pumping a widget with the SAME runtimeType and no key, `pumpWidget` UPDATES the existing State rather than recreating it! The State field `_controller` is `late final` — initialized once with `widget.sessionController` (firstLaunch). On update with the new widget, `_DmToolsAppState` is REUSED (same widget type, same position) — `didUpdateWidget` not implemented, `_controller` stays firstLaunch! So the "second launch" still shows the first controller (signedIn) → HomePage. Hence LoginPage 0.

Fix: give the app state a distinct Key for each launch in the test: `DmToolsApp(key: UniqueKey(), sessionController: ...)`. With different keys, State is recreated. That's the cleanest fix in the test.

Also — `didUpdateWidget` handling in production: not needed for real usage (single launch). Keys in test are fine.

Remaining failures (5):

1. **`SwitchListTile` not `Switch`** — cast in tests: `tester.widget<Switch>(...)` → change to `SwitchListTile` and check `.value`.

2. **"buttons show progress"** — `tester.widget<OutlinedButton>(...)` — "Bad state: No element": the OutlinedButton isn't found... because when busy, buttons are hidden (I show progress INSTEAD of buttons). My test expects the button to still exist but disabled. Design choice conflict. Two options: (a) keep buttons visible and disabled while busy (better UX honestly — layout doesn't jump); (b) change test.

I prefer (a): keep the buttons in the tree, disabled, and show a small progress indicator below. Change login page: don't swap out buttons; always show buttons + toggle, and when busy show progress and disable buttons.

3. **`notifies listeners`** — transitions.first expected `restoring` but got `signedOut`. Sequence: restore() → load() → notify with signedIn/signedOut. The listener fires only on notifyListeners — status is already `signedOut` at that point; `restoring` is never notified (no notify during restore start). Fix the test: first transition IS the restore result. Update expectation: first is `signedOut` (nothing remembered), then contains signedIn after sign-in, last signedOut. That matches implementation semantics (restoring is the initial state before any listener notification — splash is shown by the app because the widget reads status at build). It's fine — no code change needed, adjust test.

4. **widget_test 'session is NOT restored when remember-me was off'** — LoginPage not found after second launch. Why? Second launch: store empty (nothing saved). controller.restore() → status signedOut → LoginPage. Hmm, but `addPostFrameCallback` → restore. `pumpAndSetle` should handle. Unless... the first launch's LoginPage is still in the tree? No — expectation says LoginPage count 0.

Wait — maybe the SECOND launch kept showing... Let me think: `store.load()` on SharedMemorySessionStore — nothing was saved → null → signedOut → LoginPage shown. But found 0 LoginPages AND the error "nothing was persisted, so login is required again" at line 132: `expect(find.byType(LoginPage), findsOneWidget...)`. Also `HomePage findsNothing` passed? Order: expect LoginPage findsOneWidget (FAILED at 132). So neither login nor home?? Or home IS shown (login 0, home...). If HomePage were found, the findsNothing would fail after. Failure at line 132 is the LoginPage expect.

Hypothesis: after `pumpWidget(DmToolsApp(...))` for second launch, the OLD controller `firstLaunch` still has status signedIn, and ListenableBuilder of the OLD widget tree... no — new pumpWidget replaces the tree. New DmToolsApp state created → initState → postFrameCallback restore → pumpAndSetle runs frames → restore completes → signedOut → LoginPage renders.

Unless restore() returned early! My `restore()` guard: `if (_status != SessionStatus.restoring) return;` — new controller starts restoring → fine.

Hmm wait — actually the issue may be the FIRST controller: `firstLaunch` controller gets disposed? No.

Let me think about `SharedMemorySessionStore` — save was called? First launch: tap google (remember off) → signInWithGoogle(remember: false) → NOT saved → store empty. Good.

Second launch pumpAndSetle... Actually — `_signIn` finally → notifyListeners. But wait: does the tap in the FIRST launch actually complete sign-in? `FakeAuthService(googleResult: testUser())` → completes immediately. pumpAndSetle → HomePage shown — expected HomePage findsOneWidget — that assertion passed (line before 132 didn't fail).

So why no LoginPage on second launch? OH — I see it. `DmToolsApp` is `const DmToolsApp(sessionController: secondLaunch)`. When pumping a widget with the SAME runtimeType and no key, `pumpWidget` UPDATES the existing State rather than recreating it! The State field `_controller` is `late final` — initialized once with `widget.sessionController` (firstLaunch). On update with the new widget, `_DmToolsAppState` is REUSED (same widget type, same position) — `didUpdateWidget` not implemented, `_controller` stays firstLaunch! So the "second launch" still shows the first controller (signedIn) → HomePage. Hence LoginPage 0.

Fix: give the app state a distinct Key for each launch in the test: `DmToolsApp(key: UniqueKey(), sessionController: ...)`. With different keys, State is recreated. That's the cleanest fix in the test.

Also — `didUpdateWidget` handling in production: not needed for real usage (single launch). Keys in test are fine.

Fix the test: first transition IS the restore result. Update expectation: first is `signedOut` (nothing remembered), then contains signedIn after sign-in, last signedOut. So why no LoginPage on second launch? OH — I see it. `DmToolsApp` is `const DmToolsApp(sessionController: secondLaunch)`. When pumping a widget with the SAME runtimeType and no key, `pumpWidget` UPDATES the existing State rather than recreating it! The State field `_controller` is `late final` — initialized once with `widget.sessionController` (firstLaunch). On update with the new widget, `_DmToolsAppState` is REUSED (same widget type, same position) — `didUpdateWidget` not implemented, `_controller` stays firstLaunch! So the "second launch" still shows the first controller (signedIn) → HomePage. Hence LoginPage 0.

Actually, better architecture: `_signIn` when result is null → `_status = SessionStatus.signedOut` (regardless — if were signed in, a cancel flow isn't possible mid-session; sign-in only happens from login page where status is signedOut or restoring). For error path same.

Also `GoogleSignInExceptionCode.networkError` doesn't exist — use `clientConfigurationError` or `uiUnavailable` for the rethrow test.
